title: Restore standalone camera classification after successful probing
problem: A standalone RLC-510A is rendered as a redundant one-camera NVR tree because a persisted NVR kind is never reset when a successful probe later reports one channel.
reproduce: Start from a host record classified as nvr, then apply a successful validation with channelNum equal to one; the pinned baseline only assigns the nvr branch, so the stale kind survives and SideBar.qml renders an NVR header.
acceptance: Every successful probe assigns nvr for channelNum greater than one and camera otherwise; a stale standalone-camera record self-heals while real multi-channel NVRs remain unchanged.
repair: Replace the one-sided NVR promotion with a complete channel-count classification before persisting the host record.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the sticky one-sided classification on the immutable baseline and the complete red/green assignment on the candidate. The complete C++/Qt project is compiled and its four upstream test binaries are run separately in the same Ubuntu environment as upstream CI. The reporter's physical RLC-510A remains the authoritative visual check.
verification.ownerCheck: Install the branch, open the client with the RLC-510A configured, wait for a successful reconnect and confirm the sidebar shows one standalone camera row without a duplicate NVR header; also confirm any real NVR still retains its expandable channel tree.

publish.commitMessage: Fix sticky NVR classification for standalone cameras
